bugs: Email can be lost: markShipmentSent() commits status=sent before Mail::to()->queue(); if queuing the mail throws (e.g. queue backend down), the retry exits early on shipment_status !== Pending, so the customer is never emailed (confirmed with a probe). This breaks the 'email exactly once' guarantee in a narrow window.
Retry-After sent as an HTTP-date is cast to int 0 and floored to 1s, so the job retries after 1s instead of honouring the partner's delay (minor).

bugs: failed() calls markShipmentFailed() unconditionally (forceFill()->save()), which overwrites a shipment that was already Sent. If the synchronous Mail::send in notifyCustomer keeps throwing (SMTP down) until MaxExceptions or retryUntil is exhausted, the order ends up shipment_status=failed while it still has a shipment_reference (confirmed with a probe). Ops are told the shipment failed when it exists, which invites a manual duplicate shipment.
The job never checks that the order is paid: dispatching it for a pending order with a null shipment_status POSTs to the warehouse (confirmed with a probe)

Because mail is sent inside the job, an email-only retry still goes through WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited('warehouse'), using up the partner's account-wide rate-limit slots without making any HTTP call

v.rationale:
I rank impl-1 first. Both suites pass (25 tests each), both use modern Laravel 13 queue attributes, and both handle the main paths well: atomic markAsPaid with afterCommit, rate limiting, Retry-After on 429, no retry on 422, and skipping soft-deleted orders.

impl-1 makes every shipment state change a conditional update guarded on shipment_status = pending. As a result, the failed() hook can never overwrite a sent shipment or the 422 reason, and only one run can send the email. Its one real gap is narrow: if queuing the email throws right after the shipment is marked sent, the email is lost for good.

impl-2's model saves sent and failed states unconditionally. A probe confirmed that failed() turns a Sent shipment into Failed, which happens if the synchronous SMTP send keeps failing until retries run out. Ops would then see a failed shipment that actually exists, which risks a manual duplicate. impl-2 also ships orders that are not paid, and its email-only retries use up warehouse rate-limit slots. It does handle email delivery failures better, using a notified_at claim and release, but at the cost of an extra column, a try/catch, a non-queued mailable and convoluted nested conditionals in handle(). Weighting real bugs heavily puts impl-1 ahead.
